requirement_text: In order to study at Humboldt-Universität zu Berlin, you need a higher education entrance qualification (HZB). Information on the assessment and formal recognition of foreign educational certificates can be found in the anabin database. ... The Humboldt-Universität zu Berlin has applications from prospective students who have obtained their higher education entrance qualification abroad and are applying for a degree programme pre-checked by uni-assist. ... The decision on the recognition of foreign qualifications is always made by uni-assist.

requirement_text: All undergraduate degree programmes at Humboldt-Universität are offered exclusively in German. You must therefore have German C1 according to the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages in order to apply. You can prove the required C1 level with a corresponding certificate (final examination). Humboldt-Universität zu Berlin accepts all common certificates for applications: e.g. Goethe-Zertifikat C1, telc C1, telc C1 Hochschule, DSH-1, TestDaF with a minimum score of 3 in all sections in order to be able to take the DSH exam in the event of admission. Certificates of attendance of a German course are not accepted.

limitations: Applies to the uni-assist/foreign-HZB track specifically; domestic German-Abitur holders are not required to submit a separate C1 certificate. Contains a named exclusion: 'Certificates of attendance of a German course are not accepted.'
researcher_notes: University-wide for all Bachelor's/State Examination programmes (all German-taught).

requirement_text: If you have submitted language proficiency German C1 with your application and have been admitted to the degree programme, your proficiency will be tested as part of the "German Language Test for Admission to Higher Education" (DSH) prior to enrolment and commencement of studies. ... Exemption from the DSH examination is possible if you can provide proof of an equivalent examination, such as the TestDaF with a score of at least 4 in all sections or the "telc C1 Hochschule" examination passed with "very good" or "good", the Goethe-Zertifikat C2 examination passed, the DSH-2 from another German university, etc. and the certificate is not older than 3 years.

limitations: RECENCY RULE (see scalar-thresholds-are-not-enough.md trap #2): the DSH-exemption equivalent certificate must not be older than 3 years, anchor unstated (not explicitly 'from entry' or 'from application' — FAQ confirms a 5-year-old German certificate is fine for the C1 application itself, but the SAME certificate would be too old for DSH exemption specifically). A student holding a qualifying score on an expired certificate would be told 'met' by a naive scalar check when the true answer is 'must sit the DSH exam.'
researcher_notes: FAQ on the same page confirms: 'exemption from the DSH is only possible if the proof of equivalence to the DSH is not older than 3 years.'

requirement_text: At Humboldt-Universität, there are subjects with restricted admission (NC) and subjects without restricted admission (NC-free)... The selection procedure is initially based on citizenship. EU or EEA nationality: The same criteria and selection procedure apply to them as to German applicants. No EU or EEA citizenship: For this group of applicants, there is a fixed quota of 5% of the total number of study places in the first semester of undergraduate degree programmes (Bachelor's and state examinations). Study places are allocated exclusively on the basis of the average grade of the higher education entrance qualification.

requirement_text: Applicants from an EU or EEA country (Iceland, Liechtenstein and Norway) can apply for a maximum of three undergraduate degree programmes with restricted admission (NC) and also specify an additional admission-free (NC-free) degree programme. All other applicants from non-EU countries can only apply for one undergraduate admission-restricted (NC) degree programme and also apply for an additional admission-free (NC-free) degree programme.

requirement_text: Humboldt University of Berlin follows the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFR). The required minimum level for application is B2. A higher level of language proficiency (C1 or C2) has a positive effect on candidate's application. Proof of sufficient English language skills can be provided by the following language certificates: UNIcert® II-Certificate (minimum score of 1.3); UNIcert® III-Certificate (minimum score of 3.0); DAAD Language Certificate with four stars in all areas and no less than a C in any area; Cambridge First Certificate in English (FCE); IELTS – International English Language Testing System (minimum score of 5,5); TOEFL – (minimum score of 72). If you have a language certificate not listed above, please contact application@idrberlin.de to inquire about the permissibility of your specific certificate.

limitations: SCALE-AMBIGUITY TRAP (see scalar-thresholds-are-not-enough.md): page states only a bare overall '72' with no subtest breakdown and no scale/date qualifier. This unambiguously reads as the legacy/comparable 0-120 overall scale (72 cannot be a score on the new 1-6 average scale that took effect 21 Jan 2026). Since only an OVERALL threshold is given (no subtest minimums), this is NOT the partially_unsatisfiable Glasgow-style defect — ETS's comparable 0-120 overall score remains available on score reports through roughly January 2028, so 72 stays meetable today (2026-08-21). Per the trap doc's recommended interim behavior, this requirement should evaluate to needs_manual_review rather than a confident scalar pass/fail, and will become genuinely unsatisfiable-as-worded once the comparable score disappears if this page is not updated by then.

requirement_text: A language certificate is not required in the following situations: Native speakers who can show that they have spent eight out of the first twelve years of their lives in a country where English is the official language; Applicants who can provide an English language High School Diploma or English language undergraduate degree (180 ECTS or equivalent); Applicants who can provide proof of English-language coursework and examinations amounting to at least 20 ECTS credits (or equivalent), each of which was acquired as part of a course of study at a state or state-recognized higher education institution.
